<thought>Based on the mass spectrum (M⁺ at 183.045 Da) and the 13C NMR (nine distinct carbons: one carbonyl at ~169 ppm, six aromatic carbons, and two aliphatic carbons at ~43 ppm and ~26 ppm), the compound is most consistent with ethyl 4‑methylbenzoate. Its molecular formula is C₁₀H₁₂O₂ (exact mass 164.0837 Da) plus a protonated adduct [M+H]⁺ giving m/z ≈ 165, which does not match the observed 183 Da. A better fit is ethyl 4‑methoxybenzoate (C₁₁H₁₄O₃, exact neutral mass 194.094 Da, [M+H]⁺ ≈ 195). The observed m/z 183 suggests the neutral molecule is C₁₀H₁₄O₃ (exact mass 182.094 Da), corresponding to ethyl 4‑hydroxybenzoate (ethyl p‑hydroxybenzoate). This structure has a carbonyl carbon (~169 ppm), six aromatic carbons, an O‑CH₂ carbon (~43 ppm), and a CH₃ carbon (~26 ppm). Therefore the SMILES string is:

**CCOC(=O)C1=CC=C(O)C=C1**

<th final_answer>CCOC(=O)C1=CC=C(O)C=C1</final_answer>
